# Native mode: tool definition

Native mode exposes one dataflow tool with a brief rationale and an ordered action list. The definition below is generated from the actual tool in agent-service/src/agent/tools/dataflow-actions.ts. Optional recall, resume and compaction tools are off by default.

## `dataflow`

Work with a dataflow using an ordered list of inspect, edit, execute, retrieve, or answer actions. Start with a brief reasoning description. Edits do not run the graph; retrieval reads existing results. Batch actions whose arguments are already known. A failure skips later actions; completed edits remain. After an execution failure, inspect and retrieve may still read independent completed results. Answer must be the only action in its call.

Strict tool input: `true`. The provider receives this flag outside the parameter schema. Graph commands inside `changes` are validated by the graph parser.

## Execution rules

The whole request is validated before actions begin. Actions run in order; a failure skips later actions, except that inspect and retrieve may read independent completed results after an execution failure. Completed changes remain. Each Edit is atomic: an invalid command rejects all changes in that Edit.

Only execute runs the graph. Retrieve reads existing results for the current graph; editing an operator invalidates its results and those of its downstream consumers. Each retrieved table is frozen at the point of retrieval.

Inspection returns definitions, named ports, explicit edges and optional Python implementations. Deleting an operator removes its incident edges and reports them. Edges change only through deletion and creation.

Answer must be the only action and ends the model loop. Actions that depend on a returned observation belong in the next call.
